scope: Investigate the server-thread L7 SIGABRT before profiling again or closing L8
status: recurrent teardown SIGABRT; origin still inconclusive; L7 and L8 pending

constraints.game_data: fresh temporary HORIZON_HOME, launcher home and XDG paths for each run

preserved_crashes.detection_stack: glibc free -> Arc<Vec<horizon_core::geometry::Aabb>>::drop_slow in the Streaming::new<NoTerrain> worker; main thread was joining Streaming during Game teardown
preserved_crashes.other_threads: worker pools were waiting or dropping VoxelShape values; graphics threads were in driver waits

preserved_crashes.detection_stack: glibc free while dropping RenderAssets BTreeMap, reached from WorkerContext/Shared during Streaming teardown
preserved_crashes.other_threads: worker pools were waiting on condition variables; graphics threads were in driver waits

interpretation: The two differing allocator detection sites are evidence of heap corruption during or before teardown, not proof that Aabb, RenderAssets, or Streaming caused it. No origin of the invalid write/free was identified. No unsafe blocks were found in the focused game mod/runtime/Actually Additions paths inspected; this does not rule out unsafe code in dependencies or elsewhere.

isolated_reproduction_matrix.scenario: Integrated server, 1/100/1000 crushers, one iron ore input without FE on one of 1000 crushers, 40 ticks at final size; shutdown without clearing input
isolated_reproduction_matrix.result: one isolated session completed teardown cleanly; 29 1000-machine profile lines were logged

isolated_reproduction_matrix.scenario: Paired cleanup A/B: same integrated-server 1/100/1,000 crusher setup, iron ore in all 1,000 inputs, 40 ticks at 1,000; alternate two runs per condition (no cleanup vs clear all container.0 inputs and advance one tick), then shutdown
isolated_reproduction_matrix.result: all four sessions exited cleanly (2/2 no-cleanup, 2/2 cleanup); 28-29 profile lines at 1,000 machines per run
isolated_reproduction_matrix.one_variable: whether inputs are cleared and one extra tick is advanced before teardown
isolated_reproduction_matrix.constraints: taskset CPU 0-5, nice 10, six Rayon threads, fresh temporary homes per session
isolated_reproduction_matrix.interpretation: the historical teardown SIGABRT did not reproduce under either member of this pair; this does not identify or rule out the prior corrupting operation

conclusion: Historical SIGABRTs remain unresolved. The cache-isolation RSS series shows <1 KiB of measured cache structure for the crusher and similar within-process growth with or without it; the prior +8.04 MiB whole-build delta was not reproduced as cache-attributable. Teardown A/B trials with all 1,000 inputs present vs cleared both exited cleanly (2 runs each), so no cause was localized. Allocator detection frames remain locations, not causes.

later_crashes.scenario: single coal-generator session: 120 ticks, 2,380 FE, quit; reopen the same temporary save, observe persisted energy plus three startup ticks, query the block and quit the second process; abort at second-process teardown
later_crashes.detection_stack: glibc allocator abort while dropping RenderAssets -> Arc<RenderAssets> -> WorkerContext -> Shared -> Streaming -> Game on main thread. All horizon-worker threads had exited; graphics threads were waiting in NVIDIA driver conditions; control, save writer and logging threads were parked.
later_crashes.memory_check: 7.8 GiB available; no OOM evidence in kernel journal
later_crashes.limits: This is another occurrence of the same broad teardown-corruption family, now in a re-opened in-frame save. It does not identify the corrupting write or prove the mod port caused it. The exploratory game processes were not CPU-pinned; they are excluded from constrained validation.
